semin-durr:33-33.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَآئِمٌ}: «مَنْ» is a relative noun; its ṣila (relative clause) is «هو قائم». The relative noun is nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "like one who is not so, from among their partners which neither harm nor benefit." What indicates this omitted element is His words {وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ}. Similar to it are the words of the Exalted: {أَفَمَن شَرَحَ الله صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ} [al-Zumar: 22], its implied form being: "like one whose heart has hardened", indicated by {فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِّن ذِكْرِ الله}. What made its omission acceptable is that the khabar is the counterpart of the mubtadaʾ. It has also come stated overtly, as in His words {أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ} [al-Naḥl: 17] and {أَفَمَن يَعْلَمُ أَنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ الحق كَمَنْ هُوَ أعمى} [al-Raʿd: 19]. [Translator's note: the source has «منفياً» ("negated"); the sense of the examples is that the khabar appears overtly, i.e. not omitted. Translated by sense; the word as written means "negated".]

His words: {وَجَعَلُواْ}: it may be resumptive (istiʾnāf), and this is the apparent view; it was brought to indicate the omitted khabar, as was established above. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible to supply something that serves as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and to conjoin «وجعلوا» to it. Its illustration: 'Is the One who has this attribute — have they not affirmed His oneness? — and they have assigned to Him, while He is Allah who alone deserves worship, partners.'" The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "In this interpretation there is putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun in His words 'وجعلوا لله', i.e. 'to Him'; and there is in it omission of the khabar from the counterpart, whereas this khabar mostly comes as a counterpart." It has been said: the wāw is that of the ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied sense being: "Is He who stands over every soul existent, while they have assigned to Him partners?" — so the overt noun, namely «الله», was put in place of the pronoun, to affirm His divinity and to state it explicitly.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It appears that the statement is connected with His words {وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ}, as though the implied sense were: 'Is He who possesses power and oneness, and to whom a partner is assigned, worthy to take vengeance and punish or not?'" It has been said: «وجعلوا» is conjoined to «استُهزِئ», meaning: "They indeed mocked, and they assigned."

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is conjoined to «كَسَبَت», i.e. and by their assigning partners to Allah."

His words: {أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ}: this «أم» is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), implied by «بل» and the hamza, and the interrogative is for rebuke: "Nay, do you inform Him of partners whom He does not know in the earth?" Similar to it is {قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ الله بِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُ فِي السماوات وَلاَ فِي الأرض} [Yūnus: 18], where he made the fāʿil (agent) a pronoun referring back to Allah, and the referent pronoun to «ما» omitted, its implied form being: "of what Allah does not know". It was stated in that verse that the fāʿil may be a pronoun referring back to «ما», and that is permissible here too.

His words: {أَم بِظَاهِرٍ}: the apparent view is that it is the disconnected «أم». «الظاهر» here has been said to mean "the false". They cited:
286 - 2- أَعَيَّرْتَنا ألبانَها ولحومَها ... وذلك عارٌ يا بنَ رَيْطَةَ ظاهِرُ
(Do you reproach us for their milk and their meat? That is a shame, O son of Rayṭa, that is ẓāhir [i.e. vain, not sticking].)
i.e. false. Mujāhid explained it as "with a lie", which agrees with this. It has been said: «أم» is the connected one (muttaṣila), i.e. "Do you inform Him … or with an outward thing that has no reality?"

His words: {وَصُدُّواْ}: the Kufans read «وصُدُّوا» in the passive, and likewise in Ghāfir {وَصُدَّ عَنِ السبيل} [verse 37]. The rest of the Seven read both in the active. «صَدَّ» occurs both intransitive and transitive: the Kufan reading is from the transitive only, while the reading of the others can be from the transitive with its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) omitted, i.e. "and they turned others — or themselves — away", or from the intransitive, i.e. "they turned away and withdrew".

Ibn Waththāb read «وصِدُّوا» and «وصِدَّ عن السبيل» with kasra on the ṣād; this is passive, treated like «قِيْل» and «بِيْع». It is like the reading «رِدَّت إلينا», and [the saying of the poet]:
286 - 3- وما حِلَّ مِنْ جهلٍ حُبا حُلَمائِنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And the loosened garment-knots of our forbearing ones were not undone out of folly …)
It has been discussed before.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَّثَلُ الجنة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "Among what We have narrated" or "Among what is recited to you is the description of the Garden." On this view, His words {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأنهار} are an explanation of that «مَثَل». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "On this view «تجري» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referent pronoun in «وُعِد», i.e. 'promised it, with the flowing of its rivers foreordained.'" He reported from al-Farrāʾ that he made the khabar His words «تجري». He said: "This is an error according to the Basrans," and he said: "because rivers do not flow beneath the «مَثَل»; that is only among the attributes of the muḍāf ilayhi. His (al-Farrāʾ's) ground for confusion is that «المَثَل» here means 'the description', so it is like saying 'Zayd's description is that he is tall.' And «تجري» may be resumptive."

I say: what Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned, al-Zamakhsharī reported something similar to. Others reported from al-Farrāʾ two other interpretations of the verse. One of them: on the omission of the word «أنَّها», the original being "the description of the Garden is that rivers flow"; this on his part is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab — and how could «أنها» be omitted without an indicator? The second: that the word «مثل» is redundant (zāʾida), the original being "the Garden, beneath which rivers flow"; the addition of «مَثَل» is frequent in their speech, and from it are {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ} [al-Shūrā: 11] and {فَإِنْ آمَنُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَآ آمَنْتُمْ} [al-Baqara: 137]; it has been discussed before.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Someone else — i.e. Sībawayh — said: the khabar is {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأنهار}, just as you say: 'Zayd's description: brown.'" The Shaykh said: "This too is not valid: neither can «تجري» be a khabar of 'description', nor «أسمر» a khabar of 'description'. «تجري» can only be interpreted as having «أنْ» dropped and the verb made nominative, the implied form being «أَنْ تَجْري», i.e. 'their flowing'."

Al-Zajjāj said: "The likeness of the Garden is a garden beneath which rivers flow — on the omission of the qualified noun — likening what is absent from us to what we witness." Abū ʿAlī refuted him, saying: "What al-Zajjāj said is not valid, neither in the sense of description nor in the sense of resemblance; because the garden he supplied is a concrete body and cannot be the description; and because resemblance denotes the likeness between two things that are alike, which is an event (ḥadath), whereas the garden is a concrete body, so it cannot be the likeness." The majority hold that «المَثَل» here means the description, so there is no striking of a parable here; it is like the words of the Exalted {وَلِلَّهِ المثل الأعلى} [al-Naḥl: 60]. Abū ʿAlī denied that it means the description and said: its meaning is the resemblance.

ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd read «أمثال الجنة», i.e. its descriptions.

And {أُكُلُهَا دَآئِمٌ} is like His word «تَجْرِي» in being an explicative resumption, or a khabar, or a ḥāl. The disagreement of the readers over it was given in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:36-36.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: [{ولا أُشْرِكَ}]: Nāfiʿ, in one transmission from him, read {ولا أُشْرِكُ} with the nominative; it admits being cut off (qaṭʿ), i.e. "and I do not associate". It has been said it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). There is a reservation about this, because what is negated by «لا» is like the affirmative in that the wāw of the ḥāl does not directly precede it.

semin-durr:37-37.t: And {حُكْماً} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «أنزلناه». The kāf in «كذلك» is in the accusative, i.e. "Just as We made these disposed to rejoice and those to deny part of it, likewise We sent it down as a judgment."

semin-durr:39-39.t: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read «ويُثْبتُ» without doubling, from «أَثْبَتَ»; the rest read it with the doubling (taḍʿīf). The hamza is for transitivity; and the doubling cannot be for intensification, since one of its conditions is that the verb be transitive before that. The mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يُثْبِتُ» is omitted, i.e. "and He confirms what He wills."

semin-durr:40-40.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ البلاغ}: an apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) to the condition before it. The Shaykh said: "What precedes is two conditions, because what is conjoined to a condition is a condition. As for its being the apodosis of the first condition, that is not apparent, because it does not follow from it; the meaning would become: 'Whether We show you part of what We promise them of punishment, upon you is only the delivery.' As for its being the apodosis of the second condition, namely {أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ}, likewise, since the implied form would become: 'If We take you in death, upon you is only the delivery', and the apodosis of delivering the message does not follow from it — from his death, upon him be peace — because obligation ceases at death. So it needs an interpretation: namely, that for each condition there be supplied what is fitting to be a consequence following from it. The implied form: 'Whether We show you part of what We promise them, that will be a healing for you from your enemies; or if We take you in death before His creating it for them, then there is no blame on you and no reproach.'"

semin-durr:41-41.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {نَنقُصُهَا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the fāʿil (agent) of «نأتي» or from its object. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «نُنَقِّصُها» with doubling, making it transitive by the doubling.

His words: {لاَ مُعَقِّبَ}: a circumstantial clause, and it is a permanent (lāzima) one. «المُعَقِّبُ» is the one who returns upon a thing and annuls it. Labīd said:
286 - 4-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... طَلَبُ المُعَقِّبِ حَقَّه المَظْلومُ
(… [as] the wronged one who returns again and again seeks his right.)

semin-durr:42-42.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَسَيَعْلَمُ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read «الكفَّار» as a broken plural; the rest read «الكافر» in the singular, intending the genus. ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] read «الكافرون» as a sound plural.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَنْ عِندَهُ}: the generality [read with fatḥa on the mīm of] «مَنْ», and it is a relative noun. Regarding its position there are several views. First: it is in the position of the genitive (majrūr), conjoined to the word of majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla), i.e. "by Allah and by the one who has knowledge of the Book", such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his like. Second: it is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the position of [the word of majesty, since it] is a fāʿil (agent), the bāʾ in it being redundant (zāʾida). Third: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "and the one who has knowledge of the Book is more just and more decisive in word."

As for {عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الكتاب}: the adverb may be the ṣila (relative clause), with «عِلْمُ» as a fāʿil governed by it — al-Zamakhsharī chose this, and its exposition has been given; or «عِلْمُ» may be a mubtadaʾ with what precedes it as the khabar, and the clause a ṣila of «مَنْ».

What is meant by "the one who has knowledge of the Book" is either Ibn Salām, or Jibrīl, or Allah the Exalted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This view is objected to in that it involves conjoining the attribute to the one qualified, which is not permissible; only attributes are conjoined [to one another]." The Shaykh objected to him that «مَنْ» is not used as an attribute, nor any other relative noun except those excepted, and that conjoining attributes to one another is only permissible on condition that they differ.

I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya only meant attribution in meaning, not technical attribution; and as for the condition of difference, it is well known.

ʿAlī, Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Ibn Jubayr, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Mujāhid, among many others, read {وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الكتاب}, making «مِنْ» a preposition and «عندِه» genitive by it; this prepositional phrase is a fronted khabar and «عِلْم» a delayed mubtadaʾ. ʿAlī also, al-Ḥasan and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read {وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الكتاب}, making «مِنْ» a preposition, «عُلِمَ» passive, and «الكتابُ» nominative by it. It has also been read likewise except with doubling: «عُلِّم». The pronoun in «عنده» on these readings refers to Allah the Exalted alone. It has also been read «وبمَن», repeating the bāʾ that enters on the word of majesty.
[Translator's note: in the two variant readings above, the Quranic citation in the source is written as in the standard text {وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الكتاب}; per the explanation, the readings are «ومِنْ عندِه عِلْمُ الكتاب» and «ومِنْ عندِه عُلِمَ الكتابُ» respectively.]

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ}: «تلك» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being {آيَاتُ الكتاب}, the thing pointed to being the verses of the sura, and what is meant by «الكتاب» being the sura. It is also said: it points to the reports of the messengers which He related to him.
This clause has no grammatical position if it is said that «المر» is an independent utterance, or that it is intended merely to draw attention; and it is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as a khabar if it is said that «المر» is a mubtadaʾ. «تلك» may also be a khabar of «المر», with {آيَاتُ الكتاب} a badal (substitute) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). This has been set out clearly at the beginning of the book, and I have repeated it . . . .
His saying: {والذي أُنزِلَ}: several views are allowed in it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ, and «الحقُّ» is its khabar. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and {مِن رَّبِّكَ} is its khabar; on this view «الحقُّ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the truth". The third: «الحقُّ» is a khabar after a khabar. The fourth: {مِن رَّبِّكَ الحق} together are a single khabar; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥawfī. [And this is far-fetched], since it is not like «هذا حلوٌ حامِضٌ» ("this is sweet-sour").
The fifth: «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الكتاب»; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ: "and the wāw was inserted [in its wording, as it was inserted] in «النازِلين» and «الطيبين»". I say: he means that the wāw enters upon the qualifier. There is discussion in this question requiring verification; al-Zamakhsharī [allows the like of that, and holds that] there is emphasis in that. This will also come, if Allah the Exalted wills, in al-Ḥijr, at His saying {مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [al-Ḥijr: 4]. His saying "in «النازلين» and «الطيبين»" points to the verse of al-Khirniq bint Haffān, in her words when she praised her people:
283 - 8- لا يَبْعَدَنْ قوميْ الذين هُمُ ... سُمُّ العُداةِ وآفَةُ الجُزْرِ
النازِلينَ بكلِّ مُعْتَرَكٍ ... والطيِّبين مَعاقِدَ الأُزْرِ
(May my people not perish, who are poison to enemies and the bane of slaughter-camels; who dismount at every field of battle, and are pure where their waist-wrappers are tied.)
So she conjoined «الطيبين» to «النازِلين», and they are two qualifiers of a specific people. But the difference between the verse of the Quran and the line of poetry is clear: in the line there is a conjoining of a qualifier to its like, and the verse is not like that.
The Shaykh said something which entails that it is one of those in which a qualifier is conjoined to its like; he said: "Al-Ḥawfī also allowed «والذي» to be in the position of the nominative, conjoined to «آيات»; and he and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed «والذي» to be in the position of the genitive. On these two analyses «الحقُّ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. 'it is the truth', and «والذي» is one of those in which a qualifier is conjoined to a qualifier, both being for one thing, as you say «جاءني الظريفُ والعاقلُ» ('the witty one and the intelligent one came to me'), meaning one person. And of that is the poet's saying:
283 - 9- إلى المَلِكِ القَرْمِ وابنِ الهُمامِ ... وليثِ الكَتِيبةِ في المُزْدَحَمْ
(To the king, the chieftain, the son of the noble lord, the lion of the squadron in the press of battle.)"
I say: and where is the qualifier conjoined to, so that he could make it like the line he recited?
The sixth: «الذي» is nominative, coordinated to «آيات», as has been related from al-Ḥawfī. Al-Ḥawfī also allowed «الحقُّ» to be a naʿt of «الذي» when it is conjoined to {آيَاتُ الكتاب}.
In sum, there are five views on «الحقّ»: the first, that it is a first or second khabar; or [a khabar] together with what precedes it; or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ; or a naʿt of «الذي» if we make it conjoined to «آيات».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ}: this prepositional phrase is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السماوات», i.e. He raised them devoid of pillars. Then there are two views on this statement. The first: the negation of both the pillars and the seeing, i.e. there are no pillars, so there is no seeing — meaning they have no pillars, so they are not seen. The majority held this. The second: they have pillars, but ones that are not visible. From Ibn ʿAbbās: "What makes you know that they are not on pillars that are not seen?"; Mujāhid held this. This is close to their saying «ما رأيت رجلاً صالحاً» ("I have not seen a righteous man"), and like it is {لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ الناس إِلْحَافاً} [al-Baqara: 273] [and the poet's saying]:
284 - 0- على لاحِبٍ لا يُهتدى بِمَنارِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Upon a well-trodden road whose waymarks give no guidance …)
And it has preceded. This is if we say that «تَرَوْنها» is a naʿt (adjective); but if we say that it is resumptive — as will come — then it is determined that they have no pillars at all.
The generality read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the mīm, and it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); some of them express it as "it is a plural", looking at the meaning rather than the technical form. Its singular has two possibilities. The first: it is «عِماد», its parallel being «إهاب» and «أَهَب». The second: it is «عمود», like «أَدِيْم» and «أَدَم», and «قضيم» and «قَضَم»; so said the Shaykh. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The plural of «عِماد» or «عَمود», like «أَدِيمْ» and «أَدَم», «أَفِيْق» and «أَفَق», «إِهاب» and «أَهَب», and there is no fifth to them." I say: so they made «فَعُول» like «فَعِيل» in that; and this is open to question, because the patterns have their particularities, and it does not follow from «فَعِيل» being pluralised in a certain way that «فَعُول» is pluralised in the same way. They ought rather to have adduced a parallel showing that «فَعُول» has been pluralised on «فَعَل».
Then the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ "and there is no fifth to them" means that nothing has been pluralised on «فَعَل» except these five: «عِماد», «عَمُود», «أَدِيم», «أَفِيْق» and «إِهاب»; and this restriction is disallowed, for what I have mentioned to you, such as «قَضِيم» and «قَضَم». In the plural of paucity both are pluralised as «أَعْمِدة».
Abū Ḥaywa and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read «عُمُد» with two ḍammas. Its singular may be «عِماد», like «شِهاب» and «شُهُب», «كِتاب» and «كُتُب»; or it may be «عَمُود», like «رَسُول» and «رُسُل». It has been read among the Seven [readings] {فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةِ} [al-Humaza: 9] in both ways. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said about «عَمَد»: "a collective noun of «عَمُود», and the regular plural of it is «عُمُد» with ḍamma on the three letters, like «رَسُوْل» and «رُسُل»."
The Shaykh said: "This is an error; correctly it is with ḍamma on the two letters, because the third is the inflectional letter, so its ḍamma is not considered in the form of the plural."
«العِماد» and «العَمود» are what something is propped up with, i.e. supported. One says «عَمَدْتُ الحائطَ أَعْمِدُه عَمْداً», i.e. I propped it, so the wall leaned on the prop. And «العَمَد» are columns. Al-Nābigha said:
284 - 1- وخَيَّسَ الجنَّ إني قد أَذِنْتُ لهمْ ... يَبْنُون تَدْمُرَ بالصُّفَّاح والعَمَدِ
(And subdue the jinn, for I have permitted them to build Palmyra with broad stones and columns.)
And «العَمْد» is intending a thing and leaning upon it, so it is the opposite of inadvertence. «عمودُ الصبح» is the first of its light, likened in form to an iron pillar. «العُمْدَة» is what is relied upon, of wealth and other things. «العَميد» is the chief whom people «يَعْمِدونه», i.e. head for.
His saying: {تَرَوْنَهَا}: there are two views on the accusative pronoun. The first: it refers to «عَمَد», which is the nearest thing mentioned; in that case the clause is in the position of the genitive (jarr) as a naʿt of «عَمَد», and the two possibilities mentioned earlier come into it: the pillars existing but not being seen, or not existing at all.
The second: the pronoun refers to «السماوات». Then there are two views on this clause. The first: it is resumptive with no grammatical position, i.e. He cited as evidence their seeing them thus; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «السماوات», and it would be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because when they were raised we had not been created; the implied sense is: He raised them visible to you.
Ubayy read «تَرَوْنَه», having regard to the wording of «عَمَد», since it is a collective noun. Al-Zamakhsharī used this reading to give preference to the clause being a naʿt of «عَمَد».
Some of them claimed that «تَرَوْنَها» is a statement in wording but a command in meaning, i.e. see them and look at them so that you take a lesson from them. This is far-fetched, and on this view it must be resumptive, because a request does not occur as a naʿt or as a ḥāl.
And «ثم» in «ثم استوى» is for mere conjunction, not for sequence, because the rising over the Throne is not sequential upon the raising of the heavens.
His saying: {يُدَبِّرُ الأمر يُفَصِّلُ الآيات}: the generality read these two words with the lower-dotted yāʾ, following the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted. There are two views on them. The first — and it is the apparent one — they are both resumptive, to inform of that. The second: the first is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «سَخَّر», and the second is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يُدَبِّر».
Al-Nakhaʿī and Abān ibn Taghlib read «نُدَبِّرُ الأمرَ، نُفَصِّل» with the nūn in both, and al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read «نُفَصِّل» with the nūn and «يُدَبِّر» with the yāʾ. Al-Mahdawī said: "There was no disagreement over «يُدَبِّر»", meaning that it is with the yāʾ; and it is not as he mentioned, because of what I have put forward from al-Nakhaʿī and Abān ibn Taghlib.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
And «الرَّواسِي» are the firm ones, namely the mountains. The pattern «فَواعِل» for a qualifier is regular only for females; but the broken plural of what is non-rational is treated like the plural of females; and moreover its use became frequent, like non-derived nouns, so it was pluralised as «حائط» and «حوائط», «كاهِل» and «كواهل» are. It is also said: it is the plural of «راسِيَة», the hāʾ being for intensiveness. And «الرُّسُوّ» is being firm; the poet said:
284 - 2- بهِ خالداتٌ ما يَرِمْنَ وهامِدٌ ... وَأشْعَثُ أَرْسَتْهُ الوَليدةُ بالفِهْرِ
(In it are enduring [stones] that do not move, and [ashes] gone cold, and a dishevelled [tent-peg] which the slave-girl fixed firm with a pounding-stone.)
His saying: {وَمِن كُلِّ الثمرات}: three views are allowed in it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «جَعَل» after it, i.e. and He made in it, of every [fruit], two mates; and this is the apparent one. The second: it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اثنين», because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of it. The third: the speech is complete at His saying {وَمِن كُلِّ الثمرات}, so it is attached to the first «جَعَلَ», as a conjoining of single words, i.e. conjoined to what the first «جعل» governs; the implied sense being: He made in the earth such-and-such, and of all fruits. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And the second «جَعَلَ» would be resumptive."
And {يُغْشِي الليل}: discussion of it has preceded; it is either resumptive or a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of the verbs before it.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَفِي الأرض قِطَعٌ}: the generality read «قِطَعٌ» and «جنات» in the nominative (marfūʿ): either as mubtadaʾ (subject), or as fāʿil (agent) of the prepositional phrase before it. It was also read {قِطَعاً مُّتَجَاوِرَاتٍ} in the accusative (manṣūb) — and so it is in some codices — by implying «جَعَلَ».
Al-Ḥasan read «وجناتٍ» with kasra on the tāʾ, and there are several views on it. The first: it is genitive (majrūr), conjoined to {كُلِّ الثمرات}. The second: it is accusative, coordinated to {زَوْجَيْنِ اثنين}; said by al-Zamakhsharī. The third: its being accusative, coordinated to «رواسي». The fourth: its being accusative by implying «جَعَلَ»; and this is preferable because of the many separating elements in the views before it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "None of them read «وزرعاً» in the accusative."
His saying: {وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read the four in the nominative, and the rest in the genitive. The nominative in {زَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ} is by coordination to «قِطَعٌ»; in «صِنْوان» because it follows «نخيل»; and «غيرُ» because it is conjoined to it.
The Shaykh faulted Ibn ʿAṭiyya for his saying "conjoined to «قطع»"; he said: "It is not a precise expression, because in it is what is not a conjoining, namely «صِنْوان»." I say: something like this is not faulty, because it is a genuine conjoining; at most, some of it is a dependent [qualifier], and this does not impair the expression.
The genitive is in regard to «أعناب». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "conjoined to «أعناب»", and the Shaykh faulted it in the way mentioned before, and the answer to it is what was mentioned before.
Some people have attacked this reading and said: crops are not part of gardens; this is related from Abū ʿAmr. It has been answered that a garden comprises palms, vines and crops, as in His saying: {جَعَلْنَا لأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيْنِ مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَحَفَفْنَاهُمَا بِنَخْلٍ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمَا زَرْعاً} [al-Kahf: 32]. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it is said: the meaning is 'and plants of crops', so it was conjoined according to the meaning." I say: I do not know what this answer is, because whoever disallows a garden being of crops disallows it being of plants of crops — and what difference is there?
«الصَّنْوان» is the plural of «صِنْو», like «قِنْوان», the plural of «قِنْو»; the verification of this form has preceded in al-Anʿām. «الصِّنْو» is a branch which, together with another branch, is joined by a single root; its origin is "the like". In the ḥadīth: "A man's paternal uncle is the «صِنْو» of his father", i.e. his like; or because a single root joins them.
The generality read it with kasra on the ṣād. Al-Sulamī, Ibn Muṣarrif and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with ḍamma, and it is the dialect of Qays and Tamīm, like «ذِئْب» and «ذُؤْبان». Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read it with fatḥa, and it is then a collective noun, not a broken plural, because «فَعْلان» is not one of its patterns; the parallel of «صَنْوان» with fatḥa is «السَّعْدان». This is its plural of multitude; in the plural of paucity it is pluralised as «أَصْنَاء», like «حِمْل» and «أَحْمال».
His saying: «يُسْقَى»: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read it with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. what has been mentioned is watered; and the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ, having regard to the wording of what preceded, and to the feminine in His saying «بعضَها».
His saying: «ونُفَضِّل»: the two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with the lower-dotted yāʾ, in the active, and the rest with the nūn of majesty. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Abū Ḥaywa read «يُفَضَّل» with the yāʾ, in the passive, with «بعضُها» in the nominative. Abū Ḥātim said: "I found it thus in the codex of Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar", and he was the first to dot the codices. The disagreement over «الأُكُل» has preceded in al-Baqara.
And {فِي الأكل}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: it is an adverbial (ẓarf) for the preferring. The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بعضها», i.e. We prefer some of it as eaten, i.e. and in it is eating; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. And it is far-fetched in terms of both meaning and technical grammar.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ}: three views are allowed in it. The first: it is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «قولُهم» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and a qualifier must be omitted for the statement to be informative, i.e. "a wonder — what a wonder!", or "strange", and the like. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and what permitted it to begin the sentence is the implied qualifier I mentioned; and in that case its khabar being definite does no harm. This is like Sībawayh's analysis of «كم» in «كم مالُك» ("how much is your wealth?") and «خيرٌ» in «اقصِدْ رجلاً خيرٌ منه أبوه» ("seek out a man whose father is better than he") as two mubtadaʾs, because of what permitted them to begin the sentence, while their khabar is definite. This was said by the Shaykh, and there is room for dispute in it.
Moreover, there is a reason there that does not apply here: what led Sībawayh to that in the two questions is that most of what occurs in the place of «كم» and «خير» is a mubtadaʾ, so he judged them by the rule of the predominant case — unlike what we are dealing with.
The third: «عجبٌ» is a mubtadaʾ in the sense of «مُعْجِب» ("astonishing"), and «قولُهم» is its fāʿil (agent); said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. The Shaykh replied to him that they have stated explicitly that «فَعَل», «فُعْلَة» and «فِعْل» stand in for a passive participle in meaning but do not govern as it does; so you do not say «مررتُ برجلٍ ذِبْحٍ كبشُه» ("I passed by a man whose ram is slaughtered"), nor «غُرْفةٍ ماؤه», nor «قَبَضٍ مالُه». I say: and also, qualifiers govern only when they rest upon certain specific things, and none of them is present here.
His saying: {أَإِذَا كُنَّا تُرَاباً أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ}: two views are allowed in this interrogative clause. The first — and it is the apparent one — it is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), being quoted by the verb of saying. The second: it, together with what falls within its scope, is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as a badal (substitute) from «قولُهم»; al-Zamakhsharī began with this. It would be a badal of the whole from the whole, because this is their very saying. «إذا» here is a pure adverbial (ẓarf) without any meaning of condition, and what governs it is implied, explained by {لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ}, its implied form being: "when we are dust, shall we be resurrected" or "gathered". {خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ} does not govern it, because what comes after «إنّ» [Translator's note: the text has «إذا» here; the reasoning requires the «إنّ» of «أَإِنَّا»] does not govern what precedes it; nor does «كُنَّا» govern it either, because it [«إذا»] is in iḍāfa (genitive construction) to it.
The readers differed over this repeated interrogative in a widespread way, and it occurs in eleven places in the Quran; so they must be specified and the positions of the readers in them explained, for there is difficulty in mastering them which becomes easy with the help of Allah the Exalted.
As for the places mentioned: the first of them is what is in this sura. The second and third are both in al-Isrāʾ, namely: {أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً وَرُفَاتاً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقاً جَدِيداً} [the two verses: 49, 98] — two places. The fourth: in al-Muʾminūn: {أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ} [verse 82]. And in al-Naml: {أَإِذَا كُنَّا تُرَاباً وَآبَآؤُنَآ أَإِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ} [verse 67]. And in al-ʿAnkabūt: {إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الفاحشة مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّنَ العالمين أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الرجال} [the two verses: 28, 29]. And in Alif Lām Mīm al-Sajda: {أَإِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِي الأرض أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ} [verse 10]. And in al-Ṣāffāt two places, and in al-Wāqiʿa one place: {أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 16, 53; al-Wāqiʿa: 47]. And in al-Nāziʿāt: {أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الحافرة أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً نَّخِرَةً} [verse 11].
These are the places disagreed upon. As for mastering the disagreement in them in relation to the readers, there are two methods: one by reference to listing the readers, and the second by reference to listing the suras. This second is easier, so I have begun with it, and I say: these places are divided into two groups: one group of seven places with a single rule, and one group of four places, each with its own rule.
As for the first group: of it is [the place] in this sura; the second and third in Subḥān [Translator's note: i.e. al-Isrāʾ]; the fourth in al-Muʾminūn; the fifth in Alif Lām Mīm al-Sajda; the sixth and seventh in al-Ṣāffāt. You have come to know which they are from what preceded.
As for their rule: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī use the interrogative in the first and the statement in the second; Ibn ʿĀmir uses the statement in the first and the interrogative in the second; and the rest use the interrogative in the first and the second.
As for the second group: its first is [what is in Sūrat al-Naml], and its rule is that Nāfiʿ uses the statement in the first and the interrogative in the second; Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī reverse it, i.e. they use the interrogative in the first and the statement in the second; and the rest use the interrogative in both. The second: what is in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, and its rule is that Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ use the statement in the first and the interrogative in the second, and the rest use the interrogative in both.
The third: what is in Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa, and its rule is that Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī use the interrogative in the first and the statement in the second, and the rest use the interrogative in both. The fourth: what is in Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt, and its rule is that Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī use the interrogative in the first and the statement in the second, and the rest use the interrogative in both.
As for the other method, by reference to the readers, I say: the readers in these are of four grades. The first: Nāfiʿ — may Allah have mercy on him — read with the interrogative in the first and the statement in the second, except in al-Naml and al-ʿAnkabūt, where he reversed it. The second grade: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read with the interrogative in the first and the second, except the first of al-ʿAnkabūt, which they read as a statement. The third grade: Ibn ʿĀmir read with the statement in the first and the interrogative in the second, except in al-Naml, al-Wāqiʿa and al-Nāziʿāt: in al-Naml and al-Nāziʿāt he read with the interrogative in the first and the statement in the second, and in al-Wāqiʿa with the interrogative in both. The fourth grade: the rest — namely Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and Abū Bakr — read with the interrogative in the first and the second, and none of them departed from his principle. I have mentioned these two methods only because of their difficulty and the hardship of extracting them from the books of the readings.
Then the justification of the reading of whoever used the interrogative in the first and the second is the intention of intensifying the disavowal: he brought it in the first clause and repeated it in the second to emphasise it. The justification of the reading of whoever brought it once is that the purpose is achieved by it, because each clause is bound to the other, so when he disavows in one of them, the disavowal is achieved in the other. As for whoever departed from his principle in any of that, it is in order to follow the transmitted report.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قَبْلَ الحسنة}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the hastening, as an adverbial (ẓarf) for it. The second: it is attached to something omitted, as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from «السَّيِّئة»; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ.
His saying: {وَقَدْ خَلَتْ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and this is the apparent view, or it may be resumptive. The generality read [المَثُلات] with fatḥa on the mīm and ḍamma on the thāʾ, the singular being «مَثُلَة», like «سَمُرَة» and «سَمُرات»; it is a disgracing punishment. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The extirpating punishments, like the mutilation of cutting off the ear and the nose and the like." They were so named because of the likeness between the punishment and what is punished, as in His saying {وَجَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِّثْلُهَا} [al-Shūrā: 40]; or because it is taken from «المِثال» in the sense of retaliation — one says «أَمْثَلْتُ الرجلَ منْ صاحبِه» and «أقْصَصْته» with one meaning ("I gave the man retaliation from his companion"); or because it is taken from striking a proverb (al-mathal), owing to its gravity.
Ibn Muṣarrif read it with fatḥa on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ; it is said that this is the dialect of the Ḥijāz in «مَثْلة». Ibn Waththāb read it with ḍamma on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ, and it is the dialect of Tamīm. Al-Aʿmash and Mujāhid read it with fatḥa on both, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū Bakr, in one transmission, with ḍamma on both.
As for ḍamma with sukūn, it may be an original dialectal form in its own right, or it may be a lightened form of the reading of whoever gave both a ḍamma. As for ḍamma on both, it too may be an original dialectal form in its own right, or it may be by vowel harmony from the reading with ḍamma and sukūn, like «العُسُر» for «العُسْر»; and what is in that is known.
His saying: {على ظُلْمِهِمْ}: a ḥāl from «للناس». As for what governs it, Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «مغفرة», meaning that it is what governs the one to whom the ḥāl refers.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ}: there are three views on it. The first: this is a resumptive, independent statement made of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The second: {وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «هادٍ», and «هادٍ» is coordinated to something implied, i.e. "you are only a warner, and a guide for every people". In this view there is a separation between the conjunction and the conjoined by the prepositional phrase, and there is a disagreement about that which has preceded. When the Shaykh mentioned this view he did not mention this difficulty, though it is his habit to mention it in rebutting al-Zamakhsharī. The third: «هادٍ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: [you are only a warner], and he is a guide for every people; so «لكلِّ» is attached to it as well.
Ibn Kathīr paused on «هادٍ» and {وَاقٍ} [al-Raʿd: 34] wherever they occur, and on {وَالٍ} [al-Raʿd: 11] here [and «باقٍ» in al-Naḥl, by retaining] the yāʾ, and the rest dropped it. Ibn Mujāhid reported from him that he pauses with the yāʾ throughout the whole category, and he reported from Warsh that he gave a choice in the pause [between the yāʾ and its omission. The category] is every defective noun (manqūṣ) with tanwīn that is not accusative.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الله يَعْلَمُ}: two views are allowed regarding the Divine Name. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), [i.e. "He is Allah"; and this is] according to the view of whoever explained «هادياً» as being Allah the Exalted, so this clause is as it were an explanation of it. This is what al-Zamakhsharī meant by his saying: "And [it may be] that the meaning is: He is Allah, as an explanation of «هادٍ» on the last view; then He began anew and said: «يَعْلَم»." The second: the Divine Name is a mubtadaʾ and «يَعْلَمُ» its khabar, and it is a resumptive, independent statement.
The Shaykh said: "And «يَعْلَمُ» here is transitive to one object, because if [Translator's note: the text reads «لو يُراد»; the sense requires «لم يُرَد», "because what is meant here is not"] the relation is meant here; what is meant is only the knowledge's connection with single things." I say: if it is thus, it is of the sense of «عرف» (cognition), and I have put forward that it ought not to be permissible to attribute this to Allah the Exalted; I verified it in what preceded, so consider it in its place in Sūrat al-Anfāl.
His saying: {مَا تَحْمِلُ}: «ما» admits three views. The first: it is a nominal relative noun, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. what she carries. The second: it is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), so there is no returning pronoun. The third: it is interrogative, and there are two views on its position. The first: it is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as mubtadaʾ, and «تحملُ» is its khabar, the clause suspending [the operation of] the verb of knowing. The second: it is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by «تَحْمل»; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ, and this is preferable, because it does not require omitting a returning pronoun — especially according to the Basrans, for they do not allow «زيدُ ضربْت» ("Zayd, I struck"). The Shaykh mentioned nothing but this, and did not deal with this objection.
And «ما» in His saying {وَمَا تَغِيضُ. . . وَمَا تَزْدَادُ} admits the preceding views. «غاض» and «زاد» have been heard both as transitive and intransitive, so you may claim the omission of the returning pronoun on the view that they are transitive, or make it maṣdariyya on the view of their being [taken] as their maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying: «عندَه» may be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء», or of the nominative as a naʿt of «كل», or of the accusative by His saying «بمقدار», or [it may be] an adverbial (ẓarf) for the [notion of] being-settled to which the prepositional phrase is attached, because it occurs as a khabar.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {عَالِمُ الغيب}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is {الكبير المتعال}, or it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Knower". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «عالِمَ» in the accusative, as praise. Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, kept the yāʾ of «المتعال» in continuous reading and in pause, and this is the better-known usage in their speech; the rest dropped it in continuous reading and in pause, because it is dropped in the written text. Sībawayh considered its omission easy in verse-endings (fawāṣil) and rhymes, and because «أل» alternates with tanwīn, so it was dropped with it, treating it in the same way.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {سَوَآءٌ مِّنْكُمْ مَّنْ أَسَرَّ}: there are two views on «سواءٌ». The first: it is a fronted khabar (predicate), and {مَّنْ أَسَرَّ} and {وَمَنْ جَهَرَ} are the mubtadaʾ (subject). The khabar was not put in the dual only because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); here it means «مُسْتَوٍ» ("equal"), and discussion of it has preceded at the first place of this topic. On this view «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «سواءٌ», because it means «مُسْتَوٍ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak for it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أَسَرَّ» or «جَهَرَ», for two reasons. The first: putting what is in the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative noun, or the qualifier before the qualified. The second: putting the khabar before «منكم», whereas its proper place is to come after it." I say: [his saying] "whereas its proper place is to come after it" means after it and after the mubtadaʾ; otherwise his words would have no meaning.
The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and it is permissible to begin with it because it is qualified by His saying «مِنْكم». Sībawayh analysed «سواءٌ عليه الخيرُ والشرُّ» ("good and evil are equal to him") in the same way. Ibn ʿAṭiyya's statement that Sībawayh considered that weak because it is beginning with an indefinite noun is a misattribution to him.
His saying: {وَسَارِبٌ بالنهار}: there are three views on it. The first: it is conjoined to «مُسْتَخْفٍ», and «مَنْ» in that case means two persons; the mubtadaʾ, which is the word «هو», was made to agree with its wording and so was put in the singular, and the khabar with its meaning and so was made dual. The second view: it is conjoined to {مَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ}, not to «مُسْتَخْفٍ» alone. What al-Zamakhsharī said supports these two views. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "If you say: the proper expression would have been to say 'and whoever is hiding by night and whoever is going about by day', so that the meaning of equality would cover the one hiding and the one going about; otherwise it has covered a single person who is both hiding and going about — I say: there are two views on it. The first: His saying «وساربٌ» is conjoined to {مَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ}, not to «مُسْتَخْفٍ». The second: it is conjoined to «مُسْتَخْفٍ», except that «مَنْ» has the meaning of two, as in the poet's saying:
284 - 3-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَكُنْ مثلَ مَنْ يا ذئبُ يَصْطَحِبانِ
(… we shall be, O wolf, like two who keep company.)
as though it had been said: equal among you are two: {مُسْتَخْفٍ بالليل وَسَارِبٌ بالنهار}."
I say: in his expression, in his saying "the proper expression would have been such-and-such", there is a lack of decorum. And his saying "as in his saying «نَكُنْ مثلَ مَنْ»" points to the well-known line in the story of a certain man with a wolf whom he addresses:
تَعَشَّ فإنْ عاهَدْتَني ولا تَخُونُني ... نَكُنْ مِثْل مَنْ يا ذئبُ يَصْطَحِبان
(Have your supper; then if you make a pact with me and do not betray me, we shall be, O wolf, like two who keep company.)
And in the line there is no agreement with both the wording and the meaning; there is only agreement with the meaning, and that is his purpose. As for his saying "otherwise it has covered a single person who is both hiding and going about": had anyone held this, he would have hit upon what is correct; and it is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid, who held that the one hiding and the one going about are a single person, who hides by night and goes about by day so as to show his free movement among people.
The third: it is on the omission of the relative «مَنْ», i.e. "and whoever is going about"; and this only works according to the Kufans, for they allow the omission of the relative noun, and their arguing for that has preceded.
«السَّارِب» is the active participle of «سَرَبَ يَسْرُبُ», i.e. he moved about as he wished. The poet said:
284 - 4- أنَّى سَرَبْتِ وكنتِ غيرَ سَرُوْبِ ... وتُقَرِّبُ الأحلامُ غيرَ قريبِ
(How did you travel by night, when you were not one to roam? But dreams bring near what is not near.)
And another said:
284 - 5- وكلُّ أُناسٍ قاربوا قَيْدَ فَحْلِهِمْ ... ونحنُ خَلَعْنَا قَيْدَهُ فهو سارِبُ
(Every people has shortened the hobble of their stallion, but we have removed his hobble, so he roams freely.)
i.e. moving about wherever he heads, with no one driving him from any pasture; he describes his people as invulnerable and strong.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لَهُ}: there are four views on the pronoun in it. The first: it refers to the repeated «مَنْ», i.e. whoever conceals speech, whoever speaks it openly, whoever hides and whoever goes about has «مُعَقِّبات», i.e. a group of angels, some of whom follow upon others. The second: it refers to the last «مَنْ», and this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "On this view the «مُعَقِّبات» are the man's guards and armed attendants who protect him. They said: on this view the verse is about the unbelieving chiefs; al-Ṭabarī chose it, among others." However, al-Māwardī mentioned on this interpretation that the statement is a negation, the implied sense being: they do not protect him. And this ought [not] to be listened to at all: how can an affirmative statement appear while a negation is intended? The omission of «لا» is only permissible when the negated is an imperfect in the response to an oath, such as {تَالله تَفْتَؤُاْ} [Yūsuf: 85], and its detailed treatment has preceded. Rather, the meaning of the statement — as al-Mahdawī said — is: they protect him from the command of Allah, in his opinion and his claim.
The third: the pronoun in «له» refers to Allah, exalted be His mention, and the one in «يَحْفظونه» to the servant, i.e. Allah has angels who protect the servant from harms and keep record of his deeds against him; said by al-Ḥasan.
The fourth: both pronouns refer to the Prophet, peace be upon him, even though there has been no recent mention of him, and because of the earlier presence of what alludes to him in His saying: {لولا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 8].
«معَقِّبات» is the plural of «مُعَقِّب», on the pattern «مُفَعِّل», from «عَقَّب الرجلُ» when he comes on the heels of another; because some of them follow upon others, or because they follow up what he says. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The origin is «معْتَقِبات», and the tāʾ was assimilated into the qāf, as in His saying {وَجَآءَ المعذرون} [al-Tawba: 90], i.e. «المُعْتَذِرُون»; and «مُعِقِّبات» with kasra on the ʿayn would be permissible, but it was not read." The Shaykh said: "This is a gross error: the tāʾ is not assimilated into the qāf, nor the qāf into the tāʾ, neither within one word nor across two words. The morphologists have stated explicitly that the qāf and the kāf are each assimilated into the other, and are not assimilated into anything else, nor is anything else assimilated into them. As for his likening it to His saying {وَجَآءَ المعذرون}, it is not determined that its origin is «المُعْتَذِرون»; its justification has preceded, and that this is not determined in it. As for his saying 'and «مُعِقِّبات» with kasra on the ʿayn would be permissible', this is not permissible, because he based it on its origin being «مُتَعَقِّبات» [Translator's note: so in the text, whereas al-Zamakhsharī's quoted wording above has «معْتَقِبات»], with the tāʾ assimilated into the qāf, and we have shown that that is a gross error."
In «مُعَقِّبات» there are two possibilities. The first: «مُعَقِّبة» means «مُعَقِّب», the tāʾ being for intensiveness, as in «علاَّمَة» and «نسَّابة», i.e. a following angel; then it was pluralised, like «علاَّمات» and «نسَّابات». The second: «مُعَقِّبة» is a qualifier of a group (جماعة), and then this qualifier was pluralised. Ibn Jarīr mentioned that «مُعَقِّبة» is the plural of «مُعَقِّب», and likened that to «رجل», «رِجال» and «رجالات». The Shaykh said: "It is not as he mentioned; that is rather like «جَمَل», «جِمال» and «جِمالات», whereas «مُعَقِّبة» and «مُعَقِّبات» are only like «ضاربة» and «ضاربات»."
It may be answered on his behalf that he means by that that it has been applied, in terms of usage, to a plural of «مُعَقِّب», even if its origin is to be applied to the feminine of «مُعَقِّب»; so it became like «الوارِدَة» for the group who come down to water, even if its origin is for the feminine, in that broken plurals of rational beings are treated like the feminine singular in predication and in the returning pronoun. Of this is their saying «الرجال وأعضادُها» ("men and their helpers") [and «العلماء ذاهبة إلى كذا» ("the scholars hold such-and-such"); and his likening of] that to «رجل», «رجال» and «رِجالات» is in terms of meaning, not technical form.
Ubayy, Ibrāhīm and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād read «له مَعاقيبُ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "[The plural of «مُعْقِب» or] «مُعْقِبة», the yāʾ being a compensation for the omission of one of the two qāfs in the broken plural." I say: what Ibn Jinnī said clarifies this, for he said: "«معاقيب» is the broken plural of [«مُعْقِب» with sukūn on the ʿayn] and kasra on the qāf, like «مُطْعِم» and «مَطاعِيْم», «مُقْدِم» and «مَقاديم»; it is as though «مُعْقِب» was pluralised as «مَعاقِبَة», and then the yāʾ in «مَعاقيب» was made a compensation for the hāʾ omitted from «مَعاقبة»."
His saying: {مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, as a naʿt (adjective) of «مُعَقِّبات»; or it may be attached to «مُعَقِّبات», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the extent; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase occurring as khabar (predicate). On these views the statement is complete at His saying {وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ}. Abū al-Baqāʾ expressed these views in a problematic way, of which this is the explanation; it is his saying: "{مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ} may be a naʿt of «مُعَقِّبات», or it may be an adverbial, or it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in it; on this the statement is complete at it." End of quotation.
It may also be attached to «يحفظونه», i.e. they protect him from before him and from behind him. [If you say: how can two particles] identical in wording and meaning be attached to a single governing word, namely the «مِنْ» entering upon «بين» and the «مِنْ» entering upon «أَمْرِ الله»? The answer is that the second «مِنْ» differs from the first in meaning, as you will come to know.
His saying: {يَحْفَظُونَهُ} may be a naʿt of «مُعَقِّبات», or it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun concealed in the prepositional phrase occurring as khabar. And {مِنْ أَمْرِ الله} is attached to it, and «مِنْ» is either causal, i.e. because of the command of Allah — and the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿIkrima, «بأَمْرِ الله», indicates this; it is said that the meaning on this view is: they record his deeds by Allah's permission, the muḍāf being omitted — or it is in its proper meaning. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«مِنْ أَمْرِ الله», i.e. from the jinn and humans, so «مِنْ» is in its proper meaning." He means that by «أمر الله» is meant the very thing one is protected from, such as the rebellious among humans and jinn, so «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent.
He also allowed it to mean «عن», but on that there is no meaning befitting the noble verse.
It may also be attached to something omitted, as a naʿt of «مُعَقِّبات» as well; so in some of the preceding views the qualification comes with three things: their being from before him and behind him, their protecting him, and their being from the command of Allah. But the qualification by a clause then precedes the qualification by a prepositional phrase, and this is permissible and eloquent. And there is no fronting and postponing in the speech, as al-Farrāʾ and others claimed, with the origin being: "he has «مُعَقِّبات» from the command of Allah, protecting him from before him", because the default is its absence, given that it can be dispensed with.
His saying: {وَإِذَا أَرَادَ}: what governs «إذا» is omitted because its apodosis (jawāb) indicates it, its implied form being: "it is not turned back", or "it befalls", and the like. Its apodosis does not govern it, because what comes after the fāʾ does not govern what precedes it.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً}: they may be two maṣdars (verbal nouns) whose governing verb is omitted, i.e. "you fear with fear and hope with hope". They may also be two maṣdars in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as ḥāl (circumstantial); and there are then two views on the one to whom the ḥāl refers. The first: it is the first mafʿūl (object) of «يُرِيْكم», i.e. fearing and hoping — i.e. you fear its thunderbolts and hope for its rain, as al-Mutanabbī said:
284 - 6- فتىً كالسَّحابِ الجُونِ يُخْشَى ويُرْتَجى ... يُرَجَّى الحَيا منها وتُخْشى الصَّواعِقُ
(A youth like the dark clouds, feared and hoped for: rain is hoped for from them and thunderbolts are feared.)
The second: it is the lightning, i.e. He shows it to you while it is a thing of fear and hope, or it is in itself fear and hope, by way of hyperbole; and the meaning is as preceded. It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. Al-Zamakhsharī disallowed it because the agent is not the same, meaning that the agent of the showing — Allah the Exalted — is not the agent of the fearing and hoping, which is the pronoun of those addressed; so the agent of the verb given a reason differs from the agent of the reason. This can be answered by saying that the object has the force of an agent, for the meaning of «يُريكم» is "He makes you see", so you fear and hope. Like it in meaning is the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
284 - 7- وحَلَّتْ بيوتي في يَفاعٍِ مُمَنِّعٍ ... تَخال به راعي الحَمولةِ طائرا
حِذاراً على أن لا تُنال مَقَادَتي ... ولا نِسْوتي حتى يَمُتْنَ حَرائِرا
(My tents have settled on an impregnable height, on which you would think the herdsman of the pack-camels a bird — out of wariness, that my lead-rope not be seized, nor my women, so that they die free.)
So «حِذاراً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its agent is the speaker, while the verb given a reason, namely «حَلَّتْ», has as its agent «بيوتي»; so the agent differs. They said: but since the implied sense is "and I settled my tents out of wariness", that was valid.
Al-Zamakhsharī also allowed it on the omission of a muḍāf; he said: "except on the assumption of the omission of the muḍāf, i.e. 'out of willing fear and hope'". He also allowed it on the basis that some maṣdars stand in for others, meaning that the origin is: "He shows you the lightning as a causing of fear and a causing of hope", for the one who shows, causes fear and causes hope is Allah the Exalted; «خوف» stood in for «إخافة», and «طمع» for «إطماع», as in {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]. Moreover, a group, among them Ibn Kharūf, held that sameness of agent is not a condition.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ}: the clause may be resumptive, informing about them of that, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial). The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that it is a ḥāl from the mafʿūl (object) of «يُصِيب», for he said: "And it is said: the wāw is circumstantial, [i.e. so He strikes with them whom He wills while they are disputing]"; others made it a ḥāl from the mafʿūl of «يشاء».
His saying: {وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ المحال}: [this clause is a ḥāl from the] noble [Divine Name], and taking it as resumptive is weak. The generality read it with kasra on the mīm, and it is strength and destruction. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said:
284 - 8- لا يَغْلِبَنَّ صَلِيْبُهُمْ ... ومِحالُهم عَدْواً مِحالَكْ
(Let not their cross and their might ever overcome Your might in aggression.)
And al-Aʿshā said:
284 - 9- فَرْعُ نَبْعٍ يهتزُّ في غُصُنِ المَجْ ... دِ عظيمُ النَّدَى شديد المِحالِ
(A branch of the nabʿ tree swaying on the bough of glory, great in generosity, mighty in strength.)
«المِحال» is also the severest scheming and outwitting; one says «ماحَلَه مُمَاحَلةً», and from it is «تَمَحَّلَ فلانٌ لكذا», i.e. he went to the trouble of using a stratagem for it. Abū Zayd said: "It is vengeance." Ibn ʿArafa said: "It is disputation"; [and on this there is] a correspondence in meaning, as though it were said: they dispute about Allah, and He is severe in disputation.
[They differed over its mīm]: the majority hold that it is radical, from «المَحْل», which is scheming and plotting, and its pattern is «فِعال», like «مِهاد». Al-Qutabī said: it is from «الحيلة» (stratagem), and its mīm is augmentative, like «مكان» from «الكون», after which one says «تمكَّنْتُ». Al-Azharī declared him mistaken and said: "Had it been «مِفْعَل» from «الحيلة», [the wāw] would have appeared, as in «مِزْوَد», «مِحْوَل» and «مِحْوَر»."
Al-Aʿraj and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read it with fatḥa, and the apparent view is that it is a dialectal variant of the one with kasra; this is the position of Ibn ʿAbbās, for he explained it as «الحَوْل» (might), and others explained it as «الحيلة». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-Aʿraj read it with fatḥa on the mīm, as «مَفْعَل» from «حال يحولُ مَحالاً» when one uses a stratagem; and of it is «أَحْوَلُ مِنْ ذئب» ('more cunning than a wolf'), i.e. greater in stratagem. The meaning may also be: strong of vertebrae (fiqār), used as an image of strength and power, as there has come: 'The forearm of Allah is stronger, and His razor sharper'; because an animal whose vertebrae are strong is described as being very strong and able to bear what others cannot. Do you not see their saying «فَقَرَتْه الفاقِرة» ('a back-breaking calamity broke his vertebrae')? That is because the vertebrae are the pillar of the back and its support."

semin-durr:14-14.t:
And His saying: {لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الحق}: this is of the type of annexing the qualified to the qualifier, the origin being «له الدعوةُ الحقُّ» ("His is the true call"), as in His saying {وَلَدَارُ الآخرة} [Yūsuf: 109] on one of the two views. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "There are two views on it. The first: «الدعوة» is annexed to «الحق» which is the opposite of falsehood, as «الكلمة» is annexed to it in his saying 'the word of truth'. The second: it is annexed to «الحق» which is Allah, in the sense of the calling of the One called upon, the Real, who hears and answers." The Shaykh said: "This second view is not evident, because it amounts to the implied sense 'to Allah belongs the calling of Allah', as you would say 'to Zayd belongs the calling of Zayd', and this construction is not valid." I say: and where is this in relation to what al-Zamakhsharī said, that he should rebut him with it?
His saying: {والذين يَدْعُونَ}: by «الذين» may be meant the polytheists; so the wāw in «يَدْعُون» refers to them, and its object is omitted, namely the idols; and the wāw in {لاَ يَسْتَجِيبُونَ} refers to the omitted object of «يَدْعون», the pronoun referring to it as to rational beings because they treated it as such. The implied sense is: and the polytheists who call upon the idols — the idols do not answer them except with an answering like the answering of one who stretches out his two palms, i.e. like the water's answering of one who stretches out his two palms to it, asking it to reach his mouth; and water is inanimate, perceiving neither the stretching of his palms nor his thirst, and it is unable to answer him and reach his mouth. Al-Zamakhsharī said its meaning. When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned something close to that and supplied the mentioned implied sense, he said: "The maṣdar (verbal noun) in this reconstruction is annexed to its object, as in His saying {لاَّ يَسْأَمُ الإنسان مِن دُعَآءِ الخير} [Fuṣṣilat: 49], and the agent of this maṣdar is implied, namely the pronoun of the water; i.e. they do not answer them except as the water answers the one who stretches out his palm to it; and 'answering' here is a metonymy for compliance."
By «الذين» may also be meant the idols, i.e. and the gods whom they call upon besides Allah do not answer them with anything except an answering; the implied sense being as in the previous view. They were pluralised with the plural of rational beings either because of mixing — since the gods are rational beings and inanimate things — or because they treated them as rational beings in their claim. So the wāw in «يَدْعُون» is for the polytheists, the omitted returning pronoun is for the idols, and likewise the wāw of «يستجيبون».
Al-Yazīdī read from Abū ʿAmr «تَدْعُونَ», in the second person, and it strengthens the second view; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else.
His saying: «ليَبْلُغَ»: the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «باسِط», and the fāʿil (agent) of «ليبلُغَ» is the pronoun of the water.
His saying: {وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ}: there are three views on «هو». The first: it is the pronoun of the water, and the hāʾ in «ببالغِه» is for the mouth, i.e. and the water does not reach his mouth. The second: it is the pronoun of the mouth, and the hāʾ in «ببالِغه» is for the water, i.e. and the mouth does not reach the water; since in this situation neither of them reaches the other, attributing the act to either of them, or denying it, are both valid. The third: it is the pronoun of the one stretching out, and the hāʾ in «ببالغه» is for the water, i.e. and the one who stretches out his palms to the water does not reach the water.
It is not permissible that «هو» be the pronoun of the one stretching out, with the agent of «ببالغِه» implied and the hāʾ in «ببالِغه» for the water [Translator's note: the context — "the qualifier applied to other than its own" and the required overt agent «الماءُ» — indicates the hāʾ here is meant to be for the mouth; the text as written has "for the water"], because it would then be a case of a qualifier being applied to other than the one it belongs to, and whenever that is so the agent must be made overt, so that the construction would be thus: «وما هو ببالغِه الماءُ». But if you make the hāʾ in «ببالغِه» for the water, it is permissible for «هو» to be the pronoun of the one stretching out, as has been set out.
The kāf in «كباسطِ» is either a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that maṣdar, as has been set out more than once.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The kāf in «كباسط», if you make it a particle, contains a pronoun referring to the omitted qualified noun; and if you make it a noun, it contains no pronoun." I say: the kāf being a noun in [ordinary] speech is not held by the majority, but rather by al-Akhfash. By "the qualified noun" he means the maṣdar which he supplied in what preceded.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً}: either a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. willing and unwilling, or accusative (manṣūb) as an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb. Abū Mijlaz read «والإِيصال» with the yāʾ before the ṣād. Ibn Jinnī accounted for it as the maṣdar of «آصَلَ», like «ضارَبَ», i.e. he entered the late afternoon (al-aṣīl), as «أصْبَح» means he entered the morning.
And «ظلالُهم» is conjoined to «مَنْ». «بالغُدُوِّ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسْجُد», and the bāʾ means «في», i.e. at these two times.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
The two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «يَسْتوي» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, and the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ. Both are clear, in view of the fact that the fāʿil (agent) is figuratively feminine, so both masculine and feminine are allowed in its verb, like parallels of it that have passed.
And His saying: «أَمْ هَلْ»: this is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) «أم», so it is to be rendered as «بل» plus the hamza according to the majority, and as «بل» alone according to some of them; this has preceded in detail. Whoever holds that it is to be rendered as «بل» alone may draw strength from this verse, through «هَل» occurring after it: if we rendered it as «بل» plus the hamza, two particles of [the same] meaning would combine, so one renders it as «بل» alone. But it gives him no strength, for the hamza has combined with «هل» in actual wording, as in the poet's saying:
285 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أهلْ رَأَوْنا بوادِي القُفِّ ذي الأَكَمِ
(… did they see us in the valley of al-Quff, with its hillocks?)
So it is all the more fitting that it combine with it in implication. And one could say: we do not grant that this «هل» is interrogative; rather it means «قد», and a group held this, even when no hamza combines with it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {هَلْ أتى عَلَى الإنسان حِينٌ} [al-Insān: 1], i.e. "there has come"; so here it is all the more fitting. Usage has attested both the occurrence of «هل» after «أم» and its absence: of the first is this verse, and of the second is what follows it in His saying «اَمْ جَعَلوا». The poet also combined the two usages in his saying:
285 - 1- هل ما عَلِمْتَ وما استُودِعْتَ مكتومُ ... أم حَبْلُها إذ نَأَتْكَ اليومَ مَصْرومُ
أَمْ هَلْ كبيرٌ بكَى لم يَقْضِ عَبْرَتَه ... إثرَ الأحبَّةِ يومَ البَيْنَ مَشْكُومُ
(Is what you knew and what was entrusted to you kept secret, or is her bond, now that she has gone far from you today, severed? Or is an old man who wept, not having finished his tears after the loved ones on the day of parting, to be rewarded?)
And the clause in His saying «خَلَقوا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شركاء».

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَوْدِيَةٌ}: it is the plural of «وادٍ». As for pluralising «فاعِل» on «أَفْعِلَة», Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is anomalous, and we have not heard it in any word other than this one. Its justification is that «فاعِل» has come with the meaning of «فَعِيل», and just as «فَعِيل» has come with «أفْعِلَة», as in «جَرِيْب» and «أَجْرِبَة», so has «فاعِل»." I say: «فاعِل» with «أفْعِلة» has been heard in two other words: one of them is their saying «جائز» and «أجْوِزَة», and the second «ناحِية» and «أَنْحِية».
His saying: «بقَدَرها»: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «سالَتْ». The second: it is attached to something omitted, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أَوْدية». The generality read it with fatḥa on the dāl, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī and Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, with sukūn; this has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara.
And «احتمل» means «حَمَل» ("carried"), so «افْتَعَلَ» has the meaning of the bare form. He made «الأودية» indefinite and «السيل» definite only because rain falls on places by turns, so some valleys of the earth flow and not others; and «السيل» is definite because it has been understood from the verb before it, namely «فسالَتْ»; had it been mentioned it would have been indefinite, so when it was repeated it was repeated with the definite form, as in «رأيت رجلاً فأكرمت الرجلَ» ("I saw a man and honoured the man"). [And «الزَّبَد» is the scum and dross of boiling.] Al-Nābigha said:
285 - 2- فما الفُراتُ إذا هَبَّ الرياحُ له ... تَرْمي غوارِبُه العِبْرَيْنِ بالزَّبَدِ
(Nor is the Euphrates, when the winds blow upon it and its crests hurl foam on both its banks, [more generous than he].)
It is also said: it is what the torrent carries of rubbish and the like, and the bubbles it throws [onto] its bank. It is also said: it is what the valley casts out when its water surges and its waves rise. These are closely related expressions. And «الزُّبَد» is what is extracted from milk (butter); it is said to be derived from this because it resembles it in colour. One says «زَبَدْتُه زَبْداً», i.e. I gave him wealth. It is used proverbially for abundance; in the ḥadīth: "His sins are forgiven him, even if they are like the foam of the sea."
His saying: {وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ}: this prepositional phrase is [a fronted khabar (predicate), and its mubtadaʾ (subject) is «زَبَدٌ»]. «مثلُه» is a naʿt of the mubtadaʾ, and the implied sense is: and from the substances such as copper, gold and silver there is a scum, i.e. a dross like it, i.e. like the scum of the water. The point of likeness is that each of them arises from impurities.
The two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «يُوقِدُوْن» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. people; and the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ, in the second person.
«عليه» is attached to «يُوْقِدون». As for «في النار», there are two views on it. The first: it is attached to «يوقِدون»; this is the view of al-Fārisī, al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. The second: it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "being" or "fixed", said by Makkī and others. They disallowed its being attached to «يُوقِدُون» because they claimed that nothing has a fire kindled over it except while it is in the fire, and attaching the preposition to «يُوْقِدون» entails distinguishing one state from another. This does not necessarily follow. Abū ʿAlī said: "A fire may be kindled over something even if it is not in the fire, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {فَأَوْقِدْ لِي ياهامان عَلَى الطين} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 38], and the clay was not in it; only its flame reaches it. Moreover, that may be by way of emphasis, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 38]."
His saying: «ابتغاءَ»: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. seeking ornament; and «حِلْيةٍ» is an object in meaning. «أو متاعٍ» is coordinated to «حِلْيةٍ». «الحلْيَة» is that with which one adorns oneself, and «المَتَاع» is that with which they meet their needs, such as iron spades and the like. And «مِنْ» in His saying {وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ} admits two views. The first: it is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. and from it arises a scum like the scum of the water. The second: it is partitive, meaning: and some of it is scum.
His saying: «جُفاءً» is a ḥāl. As for «الجُفَاء», Ibn al-Anbārī said: "what is scattered"; one says «جَفَأَتِ الريحُ السحابَ», i.e. the wind cut up the clouds and scattered them. It is also said: «الجُفاء» is what the torrent casts out; one says «جَفَأَتِ القِدْرُ بزَبَدِها تَجْفَأُ» ("the pot threw off its scum"), and «جَفَأَ السَّيْلُ بزَبَدِه» and «أَجْفَأَ» and «أَجْفَلَ»; and Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj read it with the lām. Abū Ḥātim said: "The reading of Ruʾba is not to be read, because he used to eat rats", meaning that he was an uncouth Bedouin. I say: al-Zamakhsharī's praise of him at the beginning of al-Baqara, and mention of his eloquence, have preceded. They have justified his reading as being from «أَجْفَلَتِ الريحُ الغنمَ», i.e. the wind scattered the sheep into groups; so in meaning it is like the reading of the generality with the hamza.
There are two views on the hamza of «جُفاء». The more apparent of them: it is radical, because it remains in the derived forms of this root, as you have seen. The second: it is a substitute for a wāw, and it seems to be the choice of Abū al-Baqāʾ; and this is open to question, because the meaning of the root «جفا يَجْفو» does not suit here, and the default is the absence of homonymy.
His saying: «كذلك يَضْرِب»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), i.e. like that striking [of examples] He strikes.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لِلَّذِينَ استجابوا}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَضْرِب», and al-Zamakhsharī began with it. He said: "I.e. thus He strikes examples for the believers who responded, and for the unbelievers who did not respond.
«الحُسْنى» is a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «استجابوا», i.e. they responded with the best response. And His saying {لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض} is a new statement mentioning what He has prepared for those who did not respond." The Shaykh said: "The first interpretation is preferable", by which he means that «للذين» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «الحُسْنى» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), as its clarification will come.
He said: "Because in it the striking of examples is not restricted to the like of these two, and Allah the Exalted has struck many examples concerning these two and others; and because in it there is mention of the reward of those who respond, unlike the view of al-Zamakhsharī — so just as He mentioned the punishment for those who do not respond, He mentioned the reward for those who respond; and because his reconstruction with 'the best response' suggests a restriction of the response, and its counterpart is then not the negation of response absolutely, but only the negation of the best response, whereas Allah the Exalted has negated response absolutely; and because, on his view, His saying {لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض} would be loose, or like something loose, since the meaning would become: thus Allah strikes examples for the believers and for the unbelievers, if they had all that is in the earth; had the construction had a particle binding «لو» to what precedes it, the looseness would have gone. Also, it gives the false impression of sharing in the pronoun, even if the restriction of that to the unbelievers is known."
I say: his saying "because in it the striking of examples is not restricted": there is nothing in al-Zamakhsharī's words that entails restriction. His saying "and because in it there is mention of the reward of those who respond" to the end: from the purport of what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned too, their reward is understood. His saying "and Allah the Exalted has negated response absolutely" is not granted; rather, He negated that first response. It is not to be said: then a response that is not "best" is affirmed; because this qualifier has no implied contrary sense (mafhūm), since in reality response to Allah is never other than best. His saying "it becomes loose": how could it be loose, with al-Zamakhsharī's saying: "a new [statement] mentioning what He has prepared for them"? And his saying "also, it gives the false impression of sharing": how could this be imagined in any way at all? And how can he say that along with his saying "even if the restriction of that to the unbelievers is known"? If it is known, how can it be falsely imagined?
The second view: «للذين» is a fronted khabar, and the mubtadaʾ is «الحُسْنَى»; and {والذين لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ} is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is the counterfactual («لو») clause after it. On the first view too {والذين لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ} may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the counterfactual clause after it; and He specified those who responded with the striking of examples only because they benefit [from them], and not others.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {أَفَمَن يَعْلَمُ}: like His saying «أَفَلَمْ»; the setting out of the two views on it has preceded, and al-Zamakhsharī's position on it is far-fetched here.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين يُوفُونَ}: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «أولي», or a badal (substitute) from it, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it; or nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb, both by way of praise; or it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, what follows it being conjoined to it, and {أولئك لَهُمْ عقبى الدار} being its khabar (predicate).

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ابتغاء وَجْهِ}: it may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and this is the apparent view, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. seeking; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object.
His saying: {عقبى الدار}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the prepositional phrase before it, the clause being the khabar of «أولئك»; or «لهم» may be the khabar of «أولئك» and «عُقْبى» a fāʿil (agent) of the [notion of] being-settled.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ}: it may be a badal (substitute) from «عقبى», or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «يَدْخُلونها». Al-Nakhaʿī read «جنةُ» in the singular. The disagreement over «يَدْخُلونها» has preceded.
The clause «يَدْخُلونها» admits being resumptive or an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).
His saying: {وَمَنْ صَلَحَ}: it may be nominative (marfūʿ), conjoined to the wāw, the separation by the object making emphasis with a detached pronoun unnecessary; or it may be accusative (manṣūb) as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), and this is the weaker view.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «صَلُحَ» with ḍamma on the lām, and it is a weaker dialectal form.
His saying: {مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ} is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {وَمَنْ صَلَحَ}, and «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus. ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «وذُريَّتِهم» in the singular.
