His saying: «سلامٌ»: the clause is quoted by an implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَدْخُلون», i.e. they enter saying.
His saying: «بما صَبَرتم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what «عليكم» is attached to, and «ما» is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), i.e. because of your patience. It is not attached to «سلامٌ», because a maṣdar (verbal noun) is not separated from what it governs by the khabar; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be attached to «سلام», i.e. we greet you with peace and honour you because of your patience"; and when the Shaykh quoted this from him he made no objection to it. The apparent view is that the preceding objection does not apply to him, because that applies to the maṣdar interpreted as a maṣdar-forming particle plus a verb, and this maṣdar is not of that kind. The bāʾ is either causal, as preceded, or means "in exchange for", i.e. in exchange for your patience, i.e. for having borne the hardships of patience. It is also said: «بما صَبَرْتُم» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. this abundant reward is for your having been patient.
The majority read «فنِعْمَ» with kasra on the nūn and sukūn on the ʿayn; Ibn Yaʿmar with fatḥa and kasra, and it has preceded that this is the original form, as in the poet's saying:
253 - 8-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَعِمَ السَّاعُون في القومِ الشُّطُرْ
(… excellent are those who strive [to help] among the people, the far-reaching.)
And Ibn Waththāb with fatḥa and sukūn, which is a lightening of the original; and the dialect of Tamīm makes the ʿayn of «فَعِل» vowelless in all cases. The one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. the Garden.

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {والذين يَنقُضُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause of His saying {أولئك لَهُمُ اللعنة} is its khabar (predicate). The discussion of «اللعنة» is like the discussion of {لَهُمْ عقبى الدار} [al-Raʿd: 22].

semin-durr:26-26.t:
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ويَقْدُر» with ḍamma on the ʿayn [of the verb].
His saying: «وفَرِحوا»: this is a resumptive statement. It is also said: rather [it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»] before it. And this is open to question, in that it separates the parts of the ṣila by the khabar (predicate); and also, this is past while what precedes it is future, and there must be agreement in tense — unless it is said that what is intended is their continuing in that, and that the past, when it occurs as a ṣila, is suited to both past and future.
His saying: {وَمَا الحياة الدنيا فِي الآخرة}, i.e. beside the Hereafter. This prepositional phrase is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied sense being: and the near life, being beside the Hereafter, is nothing but a brief enjoyment. It may not be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «الحياة» nor to «الدنيا», because they do not occur in the Hereafter.

semin-durr:27-27.t: The pronoun in «عليه» refers to Allah the Exalted, i.e. to His religion and His law. It is also said: to the Messenger. It is also said: to the Quran.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين آمَنُواْ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ}: five views are allowed in it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the second relative noun, what is between them being parenthetical. [The second: it is a badal (substitute)] from «مَنْ أناب». The third: it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it. The fourth: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: "The fifth" is not written in the text:] it is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb.
His saying: {بِذِكْرِ الله}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تطمئنُّ», the bāʾ then being causal, i.e. because of the remembrance of Allah. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. tranquillity comes about by the remembrance of Allah. The second: it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قلوبُهم», i.e. they are at rest while the remembrance of Allah is in them."

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ}: there are several views on it: it may be a badal (substitute) from «القلوبُ», on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the hearts of those who believed; or a badal from «مَنْ أناب» — this on the view of whoever did not make the first relative noun a badal from «مَنْ أناب», otherwise two badals would follow one another; or a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «طُوْبَى لهم» a predicative clause; or the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ; or accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb. On these two [last] views the clause «طُوبَى لهم» is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), governed by «آمَنُوا وعَمِلوا».
The wāw of «طُوبَى» is changed from a yāʾ, because it is from «الطِّيب» (goodness); it was changed only because of the ḍamma before it, as in «مُوسِر» and «مُوْقِن», from «اليُسْر» and «اليقين». They differed about it. It is said: it is a singular noun, a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «بُشْرى» and «رُجْعى», from «طاب يطيب». It is also said: rather it is the plural of «طَيِّبة», as they said «كُوْسَى» in the plural of «كَيِّسَة» and «ضُوْقَى» in the plural of «ضَيِّقة»; and one may say «طِيْبى» with kasra on the first radical, and likewise «الكِيْسَى» and «الضِيقَى». Whether it is the name of a particular tree, or the name of the Garden in the language of India or Abyssinia, is a well-known disagreement.
Beginning a sentence with «طُوبَى» is permissible either because it is a proper name for a particular thing, or because it is an indefinite noun with the meaning of a supplication, like «سَلام عليك» and «وَيْل له»; so said Sībawayh. Ibn Mālik said: "It must be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the abrogating particles [of the mubtadaʾ] do not enter upon it." Against him is the fact that some of them made it, in the verse, accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and He has assigned them «طُوْبَى»"; and that may be supported by the reading of ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī «وحُسْنَ مآب» with fatḥa on the nūn. He said: "It is conjoined to «طُوْبَى», and it is in the position of the accusative." Thaʿlab said: "On this view «طُوْبَى» is a maṣdar, as they said «سُقْياً» ('may [Allah] give you rain')." The author of al-Lawāmiḥ accounted for this reading as a vocative, like {ياأسفى} [Yūsuf: 84], over what has been missed, meaning that «طُوْبَى» is annexed to the pronoun and the lām is intrusive, as in the poet's saying:
284 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يا بُؤْسَ للجهلِ ضَرَّاراً لأقوامِ
(… O the misery of ignorance, so harmful to peoples!)
and [his saying]:
285 - 5- يا بُوسَ للحَرْبِ التي ... وَضَعَتْ أراهِطَ فاستراحوا
(O the misery of war, which brought low whole clans, so they found rest!)
and for that reason the tanwīn was dropped from «بؤس»; as though it were said: "O their goodness!", i.e. how good they are, and how fine their return! Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of «طُوْبَى لك» is: you have attained good and goodness. Its position is the accusative or the nominative, as when you say «طِيباً لك» and «طِيبٌ لك», «سلاماً لك» and «سلامٌ لك»; and the reading of His saying «وحُسن مآب» in the accusative and the nominative points you to its two positions. The lām in «لهم» is for clarification, like it in «سَقْياً لك»." So this indicates that it is declinable and is not restricted to the nominative as a mubtadaʾ.
Makwaza al-Aʿrābī read «طِيْبَى» with kasra on the ṭāʾ, so that the yāʾ remains sound, as in «بِيْض» and «مَعِيْشة».
It was also read «وحُسْنَ مآبٌ», with fatḥa on the nūn and «مآب» in the nominative, as a past verb, its origin being «حَسُن»; the ḍamma of the second radical was transferred to the first radical with the intention of praise, as in their saying:
285 - 6-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . حُسْنَ ذا أَدَبا
(… how fine this one is in good breeding!)
and «مَآبٌ» is its fāʿil (agent).

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {كَذَلِكَ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), like its parallels. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like that sending We have sent you, meaning: We have sent you with a sending of consequence." It is also said: the kāf is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning in His saying {إِنَّ الله يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ ويهدي} [al-Raʿd: 27], i.e. "just as Allah has carried this out, so We have sent you". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What appears to me is that the meaning is: just as We have established the custom that Allah leads astray and guides, not the signs demanded [by them], so likewise We have done with this nation: We have sent you to it with revelation, not with demanded signs."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «كذلك» — [the implied sense is:] the matter is thus; so he made it in the position of the nominative (rafʿ). Al-Ḥawfī said: "The kāf is for comparison, in the position of the accusative, i.e. like Our doing of guidance and leading astray." The reference by «ذلك» is to what He described Himself with, namely that Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.
His saying: {قَدْ خَلَتْ} is a clause [in the position of the genitive (jarr) as a naʿt (adjective)]. And «لتتلُوَ» [Translator's note: printed «للتلُوَ» in the text] is attached to «أَرْسَلْناك».
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ}: this clause may be resumptive or circumstantial. The pronoun in «وهم» refers to «أمة» in terms of meaning; had it referred to its wording, the construction would have been «وهي تكفر». It is also said: the pronoun refers to «أمَّة» and to «أُمَم». It is also said: to those who said {لَوْلاَ أُنزِلَ} [al-Raʿd: 27].

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً}: its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, i.e. "it would have been this Quran", because it is at the utmost limit of soundness. It is also said: its implied form is "they would not have believed". It is reported from al-Farrāʾ that the apodosis of «لو» is the clause of His saying {وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ}, so there is fronting and postponing in the speech, and what is between them is parenthetical; and this in reality is what indicates the apodosis. The tāʾ was omitted in His saying «وكُلِّم به المَوْتى» while it remained in the two verbs before it only because it is of the type of taghlīb (giving precedence to one gender), since «المَوْتى» includes masculine and feminine.
His saying: {أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الذين}: the basic meaning of «اليَأْس» is cutting off desire for a thing and despairing of it. People differed about it here. Some of them said: it is here in its proper meaning, and the sense is: have not those who believe despaired of the faith of the unbelievers of Quraysh? That is because, when they [the unbelievers] asked for these signs, they [the believers] hoped for their faith and sought the sending down of these signs so that the unbelievers would believe; and Allah knew that they would not believe, so He said: have they not despaired of their faith? Said by al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Allah made it occur to the believers that if Allah willed He would guide all people; so He said: have they not despaired in knowledge? He is saying: knowledge made them despair, it being implied; as you say in speech: 'I have despaired of you, that you will not succeed', as though he said: he knew it with certainty." He said: "So «يَئِسَتْ» means «عَلِمَت» ('knew'); even if it has not been heard, it is to be directed to that by interpretation."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that «اليأس» in this verse is in its proper meaning, namely that, when He made their faith remote in His saying {وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً}, on the two interpretations of the omitted implied [apodosis], He said in this one: have not the believers despaired of the faith of these people, knowing that if Allah willed He would guide all people?"
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "{أَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ} may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «آمَنوا», in the sense: have not those who believe that if Allah willed He would guide all people, and would guide them, lost hope of the faith of these unbelievers?" And Abū al-ʿAbbās preceded him in this.
The Shaykh said: "In my view another possibility exists besides what they mentioned: that the statement is complete at His saying {أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الذين آمنوا}, and it is an affirmation, i.e. the believers have despaired of the faith of the obstinate; and {أَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ الله} is the response to an omitted oath, i.e. and I swear, if Allah willed He would guide all people. What indicates this oath is the presence of «أنْ» with «لو», as in the poet's saying:
285 - 7- أَمَا واللهِ انْ لو كنتَ حُرَّاً ... وما بالحُرِّ أنت ولا القَمينِ
(By Allah, if you were a free man — but you are neither free nor worthy [of it] …)
and the other's saying:
285 - 8- فأُقسمُ أنْ لَوِ التقينا وأنتُمُ ... لكان لكم يومٌ من الشرِّ مظلِمُ
(I swear that had we and you met, you would have had a day of evil, dark.)
Sībawayh mentioned that «أنْ» comes after an oath, and Ibn ʿUṣfūr made it a link binding the oath to the clause sworn upon."
Some of them said: rather it here means «عَلِمَ» and «تَبَيَّن» ("knew", "became clear"). Al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn, who is among the trustworthy Kufans, said: "It is the dialect of Hawāzin."
Ibn al-Kalbī said: "It is the dialect of a clan of al-Nakhaʿ"; and of it is the saying of Rabāḥ ibn ʿAdī:
285 - 9- ألم يَيْئَسِ الأقوامُ أني أنا ابنُهُ ... وإن كنتُ عن أرضِ العشيرةِ نائيا
(Do the tribes not know that I am his son, even if I am far from the land of the clan?)
and the saying of Suḥaym:
286 - 0- أقولُ لهم بالشَّعْبِ إذ يَأْسِرُونني ... ألم تَيْئَسُوا أني ابنُ فارسِ زَهْدَمِ
(I say to them in the ravine as they take me captive: do you not know that I am the son of the horseman of Zahdam?)
and the other's saying:
286 - 1- حتى إذا يَئِسَ الرُّماةُ وأَرْسَلوا ... غُضْفاً دواجنَ قافِلاً أعْصامُها
(Until, when the archers knew [or: despaired], and they loosed droop-eared, trained hounds with dried-up collars …)
Al-Farrāʾ rejected this and said: "I have not heard «يَئِسْتُ» meaning «عَلِمْتُ»." He was answered that whoever has preserved [a usage] is a proof against whoever has not. What indicates that is the reading of ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Ibn Abī Mulayka, al-Jaḥdarī, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and his son Zayd, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Ibn Yazīd al-Madīnī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd and ʿAlī ibn Badhīma: «أو لم يتبيَّنْ», from «تبيَّنْتُ كذا» when you come to know it. And whoever said: "The scribe only wrote it while drowsy, its original being «أفلم يتبيَّن», and he levelled these letters so that they were taken to be a sīn", has fabricated a lie.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This and the like of it is something not to be believed about a book — [the Book of Allah, which falsehood cannot approach] from [before] it or from behind it. How could this be hidden so that it remained between the two covers of the Imām [codex], when it was passing through the hands of those eminent men, careful in the religion of Allah and watchful over it, who did not neglect its major points or its minute ones — especially the canon to which reference is made and the rule on which everything is built? By Allah, this is a fabrication in which there is no doubt." Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It is said: «اليأس» was used in the meaning of knowledge only because the one who despairs of a thing knows that it will not happen, just as «الرجاء» (hope) was used in the meaning of fear, of forgetting and of leaving, because it implies that."
Two views are possible regarding «أَنْ». The first: it is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the counterfactual clause after it being its khabar (predicate), the separation having occurred through «لو». And «أنْ» with what falls within its scope, if we attach it to «آمنوا», is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, according to the disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, since its origin is the genitive by the preposition, i.e. "they believed that if Allah willed"; and if we attach it to «يَيْئَس» in the sense of «عَلِمَ», it is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects.
The second: it is a link between the oath and what is sworn upon, as preceded.
His saying: {أَوْ تَحُلُّ}: its fāʿil (agent) may be the pronoun of the second person, [i.e.] "or you, O Muḥammad, alight"; or it may be the pronoun of «القارعة», and this is clearer, i.e. a striking calamity befalls them, or the calamity alights.
Ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid read «يَحُلُّ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, the fāʿil being, as preceded, either the pronoun of «القارعة» — the verb being made masculine only because it means "the punishment", or because the tāʾ is for intensiveness and what is meant is «قارِع» — or the pronoun of the Messenger, brought in the third person. They also read «مِنْ ديارهم», and it is clear.
